doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Count Basie, Artie Shaw and the soprano experiments
title: Rehearsing Shaw's band in Buffalo and Cleveland-era band members
summary: The band rehearsed under manager Lenny Lewis before Shaw arrived, with Porky Cohen, Sonny Russo, Fagerquist and Dale Pierce, but hit a terrible business time.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So how much did you hear Artie’s band live, they only lasted that three months?

Only in rehearsal, they rehearsed quite a long time before they went out. We rehearsed the band before Artie ever got there, he had a fellow from Buffalo, Lenny Lewis who was his manager and, in-fact Lenny had a band up there that a lot of the early Buffalo musicians, not early but you know like Mel Lewis cut his teeth in that band and a few others.
And that trombone player named Ange [Angelo] Callea.

Yeah, that’s right, yeah quite a few guys. So, yeah, so Lenny was sort of a half baked clarinet player himself and Artie Shaw was his idol and so the band rehearsed and by the time Artie came in he already had a somewhat polished band plus these guys didn't take much polishing. You know we had Porky Cohen, really you know a wonderful trombone player.
Yeah right, Sonny Russo, it was a real good band, just a good all-around band. They had Don Fagerquist playing trumpet, we had Don Paladino playing lead, good trumpet player.
Yeah, yeah, wonderful trumpet player. Yeah, it was a real grade A band like Woody’s good band was.
But unfortunately it came about in a bad business time.
